Additive Lifecycle Emission Objective.condition: When carbon minimization is a primary or secondary objective and lifecycle emission factors are available for energy, manufacturing, and disposal phases. Exclude if only operational emissions matter.

Coverage-Energy Pareto Trade-off.definition: Trade off completeness of area coverage (or number of targets inspected) against total energy consumption or emissions, typically using an ε‑constraint method: impose a lower coverage bound and minimize energy.
Coverage-Energy Pareto Trade-off.condition: When routing UAVs for inspection/mapping and both coverage completeness and energy/emissions are competing objectives requiring a Pareto‑optimal set of solutions.

Spatial Heat Index Weighted Objective.definition: Use per‑pixel heat island intensity from thermal imagery as coefficients in a linear objective to prioritize cooling interventions in the hottest locations.
Spatial Heat Index Weighted Objective.condition: When high‑resolution thermal maps are available and the goal is to site green spaces, reflective surfaces, or other cooling measures to mitigate the urban heat island effect.

Unit Conversion & Consistency.definition: Convert all flows/capacities to same basis (e.g., m³/h).
Unit Conversion & Consistency.condition: Applies when inputs are expressed in heterogeneous units or incompatible measurement systems.

Big-M Magnitude & Numerical Stability.definition: Pick tight M based on real upper bound to avoid loose LP.
Big-M Magnitude & Numerical Stability.condition: Applies when Big-M formulations are used and natural safe upper bounds exist to tighten the model.

Floating-Point Stability.definition: Scale coefficients to similar magnitudes to prevent numeric issues.
Floating-Point Stability.condition: Applies when coefficients span several orders of magnitude and risk destabilizing numerical optimization.

Optimality Gap Calibration.definition: Explicitly set both relative (MIPGap) and absolute (MIPGapAbs) termination tolerances to match the objective scale, preventing premature stop with large absolute deviations.
Optimality Gap Calibration.condition: When solving MIPs where objective values can be very large or very small, and users care about absolute suboptimality, not only relative.

Numerical Stabilization Parameter Prescr.definition: When solve is numerically unstable (KappaExact > 1e12, coefficient range > 1e9), apply aggressive scaling (ScaleFlag=2), set NumericFocus 1‑3, Quad=1, raise MarkowitzTol, and avoid ObjScale‑induced dual violations.
Numerical Stabilization Parameter Prescr.condition: Applies when Gurobi LP/MIP exhibits large condition numbers or coefficient range warnings. Exclude when model is well‑scaled and solves cleanly.

Explicit Bounds for Polyhedron Aspect Ra.definition: Set finite lower and upper bounds on continuous variables even when physically unbounded, to compactify the feasible region and avoid extreme aspect ratios that cause ill-conditioning.
Explicit Bounds for Polyhedron Aspect Ra.condition: Applies when continuous variables lack natural upper/lower bounds, and the feasible polytope may become extremely elongated, leading to numerical instability and solution sensitivity.

Sensitivity Sweep for Critical Fixed Par.definition: After solving, iteratively vary a key fixed parameter over its plausible range, re-solve the MIP, and record objective value and decision changes to identify thresholds where profitability collapses.
Sensitivity Sweep for Critical Fixed Par.condition: When a model’s optimal decisions are sensitive to a few uncertain constants (e.g., mandatory waiting time) and the model can be re-solved quickly for multiple values.

Cooperative Boundary Negotiation.definition: Partition a large network into cooperative sub-areas; each area solves a local optimization; boundary flows are negotiated via shared capacity quotas and rule-based priority at interface nodes.
Cooperative Boundary Negotiation.condition: Applies when a large-scale network-flow or scheduling problem is partitioned into geographic Cooperative Areas, and flows crossing area boundaries at defined entry/exit points must be coordinated to preserve global feasibility.

Temporal Decomposition (Strategic/Tactic.definition: Split optimization into a first-stage long-term planning problem that determines baseline decisions (schedules, resource reservations) and a second-stage short-term adjustment problem that re-optimizes given realized disturbances, using a rolling horizon or two-stage stochastic framework.
Temporal Decomposition (Strategic/Tactic.condition: Applies when the problem has a planning phase with uncertain future conditions and an adjustment phase reacting to realized events, and solving a monolithic model is intractable due to scale or uncertainty.

Capacity Allocation Decomposition (Maste.definition: Central master determines time‑varying capacity allocations on shared arcs/nodes; subproblems schedule activities respecting those allocations as hard bounds.
Capacity Allocation Decomposition (Maste.condition: When a Provider of Services (PSU) centrally manages strategic flow limits on airspace corridors/vertiports and multiple operators or vehicles execute decentralized tactical scheduling.

Spatial-Temporal-Reactive Decomposition.definition: Decompose planning into a global geometric path layer, a velocity/timing optimization layer that assigns speed profiles along the path, and a local reactive layer that handles dynamic obstacles via MPC.
Spatial-Temporal-Reactive Decomposition.condition: When the environment contains static global maps but dynamic local events (moving obstacles, gate closures) require fast replanning, and timing constraints (slots, separation) must be globally coordinated.

Hierarchical Vertiport Planning Decompos.definition: Decompose the comprehensive UAM vertiport system model into three sequentially linked subproblems: (1) facility location (binary siting), (2) ground resource‑constrained turnaround scheduling, and (3) airspace flow management, with coupling through node capacity and service times.
Hierarchical Vertiport Planning Decompos.condition: When the full problem combines long‑term binary location, medium‑term resource scheduling, and short‑term corridor slot assignment, making a monolithic model intractable.

GPU-Accelerated Subproblem Solver.definition: Use Gurobi's PDHG method (Method=5) on NVIDIA GPUs to solve large continuous LP/QP subproblems in decomposition frameworks.
GPU-Accelerated Subproblem Solver.condition: When the decomposition subproblem is a large LP or convex QP with simple constraints (network flow, assignment) and an NVIDIA GPU is available, and subproblem solve time dominates.

Benders Non-Dominated Cuts.definition: When generating Benders optimality cuts from a degenerate dual, choose the dual extreme point that maximizes the cut's slack for the current master solution, yielding a Pareto-optimal cut and faster convergence.
Benders Non-Dominated Cuts.condition: Apply when subproblem has multiple optimal dual solutions due to degeneracy, and conventional Benders cuts are weak or numerous; solve an auxiliary LP to select the strongest cut.

Dynamic Programming Decomposition.definition: Decompose a problem with separable additive objective and stagewise constraints into a recursive value function, solving via backward recursion and memoization.
Dynamic Programming Decomposition.condition: When the problem can be split into stages with separable objective and transition constraints linking only consecutive stages, and the state space is not too large to enumerate.

Routing-Curvature Separation Decompositi.definition: Decompose the problem of routing vehicles with minimum turn radius constraints into a combinatorial routing phase (e.g., TSP, VRP) using straight-line distances, followed by a curvature-smoothing phase that replaces sharp turns with Dubins arcs and generates a flyable trajectory, possibly with local re-optimization of segment connections.
Routing-Curvature Separation Decompositi.condition: When vehicles have Dubins (minimum turn radius) motion constraints and the integrated problem is too complex for direct MILP; applicable when turn costs are significant but sequencing is the primary combinatorial challenge.

Pre-Assignment Enumeration Reduction.definition: Convert a nonlinear or mixed-integer problem with interacting discrete design variables and continuous flows into a pure selection problem by pre-enumerating all feasible discrete assignments, precomputing optimal flows or bounds for each, and using binary variables to choose among the precomputed scenarios.
Pre-Assignment Enumeration Reduction.condition: When the number of discrete design scenarios (e.g., service level assignments across all nodes) is tractable for exhaustive enumeration, and the remaining subproblem is a linear program or network flow that can be solved offline.

MIP Optimality and Feasibility Caveat.definition: MIP solvers may stop with a time limit or gap, not a proven global optimum; treat the solution as heuristic-optimal and check for numerical infeasibility.
MIP Optimality and Feasibility Caveat.condition: When solving large mixed-integer programs where an optimality proof is impractical, and numerical issues may cause constraint violations beyond tolerance.

Perturbation Robustness Sensitivity Test.definition: Repeatedly solve the model after adding small random noise to the objective coefficients and right‑hand sides, then measure the maximum violation of primal/dual feasibility and the change in objective value.
Perturbation Robustness Sensitivity Test.condition: When the feasible region is thin (near‑parallel constraints) or ill‑conditioned, and modelers need to know whether the optimal solution is practically reliable under small data errors.

Avoid Monolithic MILP for Integrated Tru.definition: Pure mixed‑integer linear programming formulations that simultaneously decide truck routes, drone routes, and synchronization constraints are only solvable to proven optimality for very small instances (≤ 11 customers). For realistic sizes, use decomposition, matheuristics, or column generation.
Avoid Monolithic MILP for Integrated Tru.condition: When the integrated truck‑drone routing problem (FSTSP, PDSTSP, two‑echelon) has more than about 10–15 customer nodes.

Newton Local Optimum Risk.definition: When the residual of a nonlinear continuum equilibrium model is non‑convex, Newton‑based iterations can converge to a local (not global) optimum. Robustness requires multiple starting points or global search.
Newton Local Optimum Risk.condition: When using Newton iteration to solve for system optimum or user equilibrium in continuum flow models with congestion, and the solution space may contain multiple local equilibria.

Library Import/Reference Errors.definition: Import solver correctly, e.g., `import gurobipy as gp`.
Library Import/Reference Errors.condition: Applies when the mathematical model contains solver calls that fail due to missing or incorrectly referenced libraries or aliases.

Quicksum vs. sum Syntax.definition: `gp.quicksum()` builds expressions efficiently; Python `sum()` is slow.
Quicksum vs. sum Syntax.condition: Applies when the mathematical model contains linear expressions aggregated over large index sets that should be constructed using solver-native summation operators.

Strict Inequalities.definition: Replace x < y with x ≤ y - 1 for integer vars, or add ε-buffer for continuous.
Strict Inequalities.condition: Applies when the mathematical model contains strict inequality relations between variables that cannot be directly handled by LP/MIP solvers.

Multi‑Scenario Feature (NumScenarios, Sc.definition: Use Gurobi's built‑in multi‑scenario support to solve stochastic programs with discrete scenarios by setting NumScenarios and modifying scenario‑specific RHS, objective coefficients, and variable upper bounds.
Multi‑Scenario Feature (NumScenarios, Sc.condition: When a stochastic LP/MIP has a manageable number of scenarios and the objective is to minimize sum of scenario objectives or a weighted sum; Gurobi's native multi‑scenario interface avoids duplicating the model.

Lazy Model Update & Bulk Attribute Acces.definition: Call model.update() only after model construction and before querying attributes if no optimization has occurred; use bulk getAttr/setAttr methods for arrays to reduce overhead.
Lazy Model Update & Bulk Attribute Acces.condition: When building a Gurobi model programmatically and retrieving variable/constraint attributes before calling optimize, or when collecting many attribute values post‑solve.

Avoid reset() to Preserve Warm Start.definition: Do not call model.reset() between successive solves when only bounds/coefficients have been modified; the solver automatically reuses the previous basis as a warm start. Calling reset() clears the warm‑start information, forcing optimization from scratch.

Tupledict Wildcard Summation.definition: Use the .sum() method on a Gurobi tupledict (from addVars) with '*' wildcard to sum over all values of an index, and specific keys for other indices, to build concise constraints.
Tupledict Wildcard Summation.condition: Applies when variables are created with addVars over multiple index sets and summation over one index is needed while fixing others, avoiding manual loops.

addVars with obj Argument.definition: Pass the cost coefficient dictionary as the obj parameter when calling m.addVars(keys, obj=cost_dict) to automatically set the linear objective for each variable.
addVars with obj Argument.condition: When each variable has a known cost coefficient that can be stored in a dictionary with keys matching the variable indices, enabling concise model construction and reducing manual objective building.

Data Preparation with gp.multidict and g.definition: Use gp.multidict to convert a Python dict of tuples into a Gurobi tupledict and a list of keys, enabling concise variable creation and summation. Use gp.tuplelist to maintain a list of eligible tuples for quick filtering.
Data Preparation with gp.multidict and g.condition: When model data is naturally keyed by tuples (e.g., worker‑shift pairs) and you need to iterate over all allowed combinations or build constraints with sparse sets.

FeasRelax for Minimal Infeasibility Repa.definition: Use Gurobi’s feasRelax() to automatically add slack/surplus variables to all constraints and minimize their weighted sum (L1 penalty), yielding a minimal adjustment to make an infeasible model feasible.
FeasRelax for Minimal Infeasibility Repa.condition: When a MIP is infeasible due to tight deadline, slot, or capacity constraints and you want the smallest total violation to restore feasibility without manually creating slacks.

Batch Model Submission for Many Instance.definition: Submit multiple independent Gurobi models together for solution on a cluster or local parallel pool, using the batch interface to reduce total wall-clock time.
Batch Model Submission for Many Instance.condition: When a large number of structurally identical MILPs must be solved with different parameter values (e.g., scenario analysis, Monte Carlo simulation) and a cluster or multi-core machine is available.

Programmatic Coefficient Update Synchron.definition: When modifying variable bounds, constraint coefficients, or objective coefficients programmatically after model construction but before re-solving, the changes do not take effect until update() or optimize() is called.
Programmatic Coefficient Update Synchron.condition: Applies when building iterative repair heuristics, column generation, or any loop that modifies model data between solves. Exclude for one-shot model builds with no mid-solve modifications.

Time-Limited IIS Completeness Check.definition: When IIS computation is terminated by a time limit, the result is an approximate (possibly non-minimal) subsystem; always verify the IISMinimal attribute to confirm exactness before acting on the diagnosis.
Time-Limited IIS Completeness Check.condition: Apply when using time-limited IIS computation on large models where computeIIS() may not finish. Exclude when IIS computation completes within the time limit naturally.

NonConvex=2 for Global Quadratics.definition: When the model contains bilinear terms (x*y) or nonconvex quadratic constraints, set the Gurobi parameter NonConvex=2 to enable global optimization via spatial branch‑and‑bound.
NonConvex=2 for Global Quadratics.condition: When solving a model with nonconvex quadratic constraints, e.g., battery power = V*I or P = U^2/R, and global optimality is needed.

Prefer Modern addGenConstr Functions.definition: Use Gurobi's addGenConstrMax, addGenConstrMin, addGenConstrAbs, addGenConstrOr, addGenConstrAnd instead of deprecated addMax, addMin, addAbs, etc.
Prefer Modern addGenConstr Functions.condition: When writing Gurobi code in version 10 or later and modeling max/min/abs/and/or constraints.

Solver-Native Multi-Objective Control.definition: Use solver-provided multi-objective methods (e.g., Gurobi's setObjectiveN) to define lexicographic objectives with priorities and weights, avoiding manual epsilon-constraint loops.
Solver-Native Multi-Objective Control.condition: When multiple objectives with strict priority ordering must be optimized, and the solver supports native multi-objective optimization (Gurobi 9+). Exclude when objectives have no priority or when a single weighted sum suffices.

Matrix-Vector Compact Constraint Formula.definition: Use MVar objects with addMVar and matrix multiplication @ with addMConstr to impose indexed constraints in compact vectorized form, replacing explicit loops.
Matrix-Vector Compact Constraint Formula.condition: When a Gurobi Python model contains repeated linear constraints over large index sets (flow conservation, capacity coupling, time-linking) and the coefficient structure is expressible as matrix operations.

Batch Coefficient Modification with Obje.definition: Accumulate all bound, RHS, and coefficient changes between explicit update() calls; modifying after each change is expensive. Use Var/Constr object handles rather than numeric indices after modifications.
Batch Coefficient Modification with Obje.condition: When modifying model parameters (variable bounds, constraint RHS, objective coefficients) in iterative loops such as column generation, repair heuristics, or re-optimization with changing data.

Sparse Linear Constraint API for Speed.definition: Use addLConstr (Gurobi's low-level sparse constraint addition) instead of addConstr when adding constraints with very few nonzero coefficients per row to gain up to 50% construction speed.
Sparse Linear Constraint API for Speed.condition: When building models programmatically with many linear constraints where each row has sparse structure (e.g., 1–5 nonzeros), such as assignment or network flow constraints.

Degeneracy Cycling Prevention via Simple.definition: Select a simplex pivoting rule that avoids cycling when many degenerate basic solutions exist, e.g., Bland's rule or lexicographic ordering.
Degeneracy Cycling Prevention via Simple.condition: When solving LPs with many tight constraints causing degenerate vertices, and standard simplex may stall or cycle.

Dual Simplex Re-optimization with Reduce.definition: After adding constraints or variables to an optimal LP, re‑solve using dual simplex from the previous basis and then fix nonbasic variables whose reduced cost exceeds the optimality gap.
Dual Simplex Re-optimization with Reduce.condition: When modifying a model with new cuts or columns in iterative decomposition algorithms (Benders, column generation).

Candidate List Pivoting and Reinversion.definition: When using the simplex method on large-scale network LPs, use candidate list pivoting to reduce per-iteration column scans, and set a reinversion frequency to periodically recompute the basis inverse with high numerical accuracy.
Candidate List Pivoting and Reinversion.condition: Applies when solving minimum-cost flow, multi-commodity flow, or large transportation LPs with the primal simplex method; model size exceeds ~100k constraints and simplex iterations slow due to full pricing or numerical degradation.

Barrier Method for Degenerate Large-Scal.definition: Switch from simplex to primal-dual interior-point (barrier) method when solving linear programs with high degeneracy and large size, because barrier is unaffected by degenerate cycling and scales polynomially.
Barrier Method for Degenerate Large-Scal.condition: Apply when a network flow or allocation LP has many degenerate pivots (stalling), size exceeds 500k constraints, and a crossover to a basic solution is not strictly required. Exclude when dual values must correspond to a unique optimal basis (basis needed for sensitivity analysis) unless crossover is enabled.

Warm-Start Basis Reuse for Model Modific.definition: When modifying a solved LP (adding a variable, constraint, or perturbing a column), use the current basis and dual information to decide whether to re‑optimize and to select the starting simplex method; avoids solving from scratch.
Warm-Start Basis Reuse for Model Modific.condition: When an LP has been solved to optimality and then undergoes structural changes (new variable, new inequality, column perturbation); the solver supports basis warm‑start and dual/primal simplex re‑optimization.

KeyError & Index Mismatch.definition: Attempting to access non-existent dict entry; fix by `.get()` or validation.
KeyError & Index Mismatch.condition: Applies when the mathematical model contains indexed variables or parameters that are accessed with indices not present in the corresponding data structures.

Missing Data Defaults.definition: Provide default 0 when optional parameter absent to avoid `None`.
Missing Data Defaults.condition: Applies when the mathematical model contains optional parameters whose values may be absent in the dataset and require default assignments to preserve model validity.

Flat Scalar Index and ASCII Naming Requi.definition: Indices passed to addVars must be scalar types (int, str), never nested tuples. Constraint names must contain only ASCII characters without spaces.
Flat Scalar Index and ASCII Naming Requi.condition: When using gurobipy to build models programmatically with index sets stored as tuples or when naming constraints for LP file export.

Callback-Driven Lazy Constraint Addition.definition: Add constraints dynamically via solver callback when a candidate integer solution violates them, avoiding enumerating exponentially many inequalities upfront.
Callback-Driven Lazy Constraint Addition.condition: When a problem (like TSP/VRP) requires an exponential family of cuts (subtour elimination) that would be too large to include in the initial model, use a MIPSOL callback to detect violation and inject the cut only when needed.
Callback-Driven Lazy Constraint Addition.explanation: Build the base model with only assignment constraints (e.g., degree‑2 for TSP). In a MIPSOL callback, check each incumbent solution for subtours; if found, add a lazy constraint Σ_{i∈S, j∉S} x_ij ≥ 2 (or 1 for directed). The solver then re‑optimizes, and the process repeats until no subtour remains. This drastically reduces the model size.

User Cut Addition in MIPNODE Callback.definition: Add valid inequalities (user cuts) only in the MIPNODE callback, not MIPSOL; lazy constraints belong in MIPSOL. User cuts must not cut off any integer feasible solutions.
User Cut Addition in MIPNODE Callback.condition: When you want to add cuts that tighten the LP relaxation (e.g., cover cuts, clique inequalities) that are valid for all integer solutions but not for fractional ones. Exclude when the cut requires checking full integer solution feasibility (use lazy).
User Cut Addition in MIPNODE Callback.explanation: MIPNODE callback fires after solving the node LP relaxation, allowing injection of user cuts via cbCut(). These cuts are added to the node LP and propagated. Lazy constraints are added only in MIPSOL when an integer feasible solution violates a logical constraint; adding user cuts in MIPSOL may be inefficient or ignored.
User Cut Addition in MIPNODE Callback.example: In a vehicle routing model, after solving node LP, detect fractional subtours and add cut requiring at least 2 exits from that set. Use cbCut() inside MIPNODE. For full subtour checking of integer solutions, use MIPSOL and cbLazy.

MIP-Start Injection from Heuristic.definition: Set initial solution (Start attribute) for binary variables using a simple heuristic to warm‑start the MIP solver.
MIP-Start Injection from Heuristic.condition: When the MIP has many binary variables and a greedy or rule‑based heuristic can quickly construct a feasible solution; setting it as a MIP start can reduce branch‑and‑bound time significantly.

Fix-and-Dive Primal Heuristic.definition: Iteratively solve LP relaxation, fix variables with values close to integer, re‑solve the reduced MIP to obtain a feasible integer solution quickly.
Fix-and-Dive Primal Heuristic.condition: When a large MIP lacks a primal bound and the LP relaxation yields many fractional variables that are near-integer; the heuristic can provide a high-quality feasible solution or warm start.

Solution Pool Utilization.definition: Collect multiple distinct feasible solutions from the solver’s solution pool to enable post‑optimization selection based on unmodeled criteria or robustness analysis.
Solution Pool Utilization.condition: When the optimization problem has many equally good or near‑optimal solutions and the decision-maker wants to evaluate robustness, equity, or implement qualitative preferences after solving.
Solution Pool Utilization.explanation: Set PoolSearchMode=2 to perform a systematic search for the N best solutions, and define a PoolGap to control how close solutions must be to the best. Retrieve solutions via the SolPoolObjVal and SolPool attributes. This is more efficient than repeated solve‑and‑forbid, and yields a diverse set of near‑optimal plans.
Solution Pool Utilization.example:
model.setParam('PoolSearchMode', 2)  # systematic search
model.setParam('PoolGap', 0.05)        # 5% tolerance
model.optimize()
nSolutions = model.SolCount
for i in range(nSolutions):
    model.setParam('SolutionNumber', i)
    print(model.PoolObjVal)

Deconfliction via Solution Pool.definition: Collect multiple distinct, conflict‑free solutions by enabling the solution pool with PoolSearchMode=2 and zero PoolGap, allowing post‑solve selection of alternative deconfliction plans.
Deconfliction via Solution Pool.condition: When the problem includes aircraft/vehicle separation constraints and the decision‑maker needs a set of alternative feasible schedules rather than a single optimum.

Scenario-Contingent Variable Upper Bound.definition: Use Gurobi’s multi‑scenario attribute ScenNUB to set the upper bound of a binary or continuous variable to zero in specific scenarios, effectively making an asset unavailable without adding extra constraints.
Scenario-Contingent Variable Upper Bound.condition: When using Gurobi’s native multi‑scenario interface (NumScenarios) and a variable (e.g., open[p]) must be forced to zero in some discrete scenarios.

Efficient Constraint Addition using Gene.definition: Use addConstrs with a generator expression that yields (lhs, sense, rhs) tuples to add many constraints in one call, avoiding repeated addConstr.
Efficient Constraint Addition using Gene.condition: When building a model with hundreds of similar indexed constraints, such as capacity or demand balance equations.

Data-Model Separation for Reusability.definition: Keep all problem data (costs, demands, capacities) in separate Python dictionaries or DataFrames loaded from external files; the model construction code references these variables without hard‑coded numbers.
Data-Model Separation for Reusability.condition: When the optimization model will be reused with different input datasets or when data changes frequently.

Callback-Based Primal Heuristic Injectio.definition: During MIP solving, use a callback to read the LP relaxation solution, round fractional values, and inject a feasible integer solution, while disabling standard heuristics to rely on the custom heuristic.
Callback-Based Primal Heuristic Injectio.condition: When solving a large MIP with many binary variables, the LP relaxation yields fractional solutions that are easily rounded to feasible integer points, and the solver's default heuristics are ineffective or need to be overridden.

Solver Tuning Sensitivity.definition: Solver parameters (heuristics, cuts, branching) tuned for one problem class often degrade on structurally different instances; re-tuning is necessary when constraints, variables, or objectives change significantly.
Solver Tuning Sensitivity.condition: When solving large MILPs and relying on parameter tuning to achieve acceptable solve times.

Constraint-Guided Primal Heuristic.definition: Temporarily fix a subset of binary variables to plausible values (via bounds or equality constraints) to steer a primal heuristic (e.g., NoRel) to a feasible solution quickly; then use that solution as a MIP start after restoring original bounds.
Constraint-Guided Primal Heuristic.condition: When a large MIP has difficulty finding any feasible solution, but domain knowledge provides a trustworthy partial assignment (e.g., certain vehicles should serve certain missions). Exclude when the hint could lock the heuristic into an infeasible subspace with no recovery.

Presolve-Induced Dual Invisibility.definition: Presolve may eliminate constraints, making dual values (shadow prices) inaccessible for the original model. Disable presolve when duals are needed for pricing or decomposition.
Presolve-Induced Dual Invisibility.condition: When you must extract dual values from an LP or MIP relaxation (e.g., for Benders cuts, marginal cost analysis).

Presolve-Altered Integrality Structure.definition: Presolve may eliminate rows, columns, or tighten bounds, thereby changing which variables appear as integer in the presolved model, potentially affecting integrality‑based cuts and branching priority.
Presolve-Altered Integrality Structure.condition: When integrality of certain variables is critical (e.g., for cut generation or dual interpretation), and presolve might remove them. Exclude when all integer variables are essential and presolve does not alter integrality, or when duals are not needed.
Presolve-Altered Integrality Structure.explanation: Presolve can fix integer variables to bounds, reduce their domains, or drop them entirely. This can cause custom cuts or logic that expects certain variables to remain integer to fail. Always verify the number of integer variables before and after presolve, and disable presolve (Presolve=0) if integrality structure must be preserved exactly.
Presolve-Altered Integrality Structure.example:
orig_numint = model.NumInt
model.optimize()
if model.NumInt < orig_numint: print('Presolve eliminated some integer variables') - disable presolve if that breaks logic.

Multi-Start for Nonconvex NLP.definition: When using a barrier solver for a nonconvex NLP (local optimality only), run from multiple distinct starting points and keep the best objective to improve global optimality confidence.
Multi-Start for Nonconvex NLP.condition: When solving a nonconvex NLP where global optimality is important and the barrier solver may converge to different local minima depending on the starting point.

Callback Interface Compatibility.definition: Ensure the modeling language and solver deployment environment support callbacks; Gurobi callbacks are not available in MATLAB or R, and have restrictions in Compute Server and Instant Cloud deployments.
Callback Interface Compatibility.condition: When the optimization model relies on callbacks for lazy constraint addition, heuristic injection, or custom termination, and the chosen interface or deployment may lack callback support.

Fixed MIP Dual Extraction.definition: Fix integer variables at their optimal values and solve the resulting continuous LP to obtain dual values for constraints; interpret duals as conditional on the chosen discrete configuration.
Fixed MIP Dual Extraction.condition: When shadow prices of capacity constraints are needed for a mixed-integer model but MIP solvers do not provide duals; duals from the fixed continuous model reflect marginal values under the fixed discrete decisions only.

Multi-Scenario Baseline Robustness Test.definition: Fix a candidate baseline plan (by setting variable bounds to the plan's values) and use the solver's multi-scenario feature (NumScenarios, ScenNRhs) to evaluate performance under many discrete uncertain scenarios in one solve.
Multi-Scenario Baseline Robustness Test.condition: When an operational baseline plan must be stress-tested against a set of uncertain demand, weather, or capacity scenarios to gauge robustness without re-optimizing the full MIP repeatedly.

Exact Condition Number Monitoring (Kappa.definition: After solving an LP or MIP, check the solver's exact condition number attribute (e.g., Gurobi KappaExact) to assess numerical stability of the optimal basis.
Exact Condition Number Monitoring (Kappa.condition: When solution quality is suspect (large objective jumps, infeasibility reports at solution) or when coefficients span many orders of magnitude.

Presolve Disable for Raw Solver Behavior.definition: Set Presolve=0 during numerical‑stability debugging and scaling tests to prevent presolve from applying transformations that could mask the inherent conditioning of the original formulation.
Presolve Disable for Raw Solver Behavior.condition: When investigating numerical issues or testing the effect of scaling; presolve may automatically scale or eliminate constraints, obscuring the raw model's sensitivity. Do not disable presolve in production runs unless necessary for duals.

Reduced‑Price Fixing Heuristic.definition: After solving the LP relaxation, fix integer variables to their current values if their reduced cost exceeds the current optimality gap, safely reducing problem size.
Reduced‑Price Fixing Heuristic.condition: When solving a MIP with a primal bound and an optimality gap; exclusion when reduced costs are unavailable (e.g., MIP without LP relaxation).

Auxiliary Binary for Strong Branching.definition: Add a binary variable that captures a natural operational dichotomy (e.g., peak load reached) even if not required, linking it via indicator constraints to provide strong branching candidates.
Auxiliary Binary for Strong Branching.condition: When MIP branching on existing binaries is weak and the solver struggles. Identify a logical state that cleanly partitions the solution space.

Network Flow Reformulation for Efficienc.definition: Recognize that a linear program with only flow conservation and arc capacity constraints can be modeled as a minimum-cost network flow (transshipment) problem, enabling the use of specialized network simplex algorithms that are much faster than general LP simplex.
Network Flow Reformulation for Efficienc.condition: Applies when the LP consists solely of node balance equations (inflow - outflow = net supply) and upper/lower bounds on arcs, with no side constraints. Exclude if extra constraints (e.g., quality blending, fixed charge) disrupt the pure network structure.

Sensitivity Sweep for Critical Fixed Par.definition: After solving, iteratively vary a key fixed parameter over its plausible range, re-solve the MIP, and record objective value and decision changes to identify thresholds where profitability collapses.
Sensitivity Sweep for Critical Fixed Par.condition: When a model’s optimal decisions are sensitive to a few uncertain constants (e.g., mandatory waiting time) and the model can be re-solved quickly for multiple values.
